llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent LMail tooling, but it can send stored credentials to any configured base URL without endpoint validation, including for admin workflows.

dimensions.detail: Network access and credentials are expected for LMail, but authenticated requests use a user/environment-controlled base URL without requiring HTTPS, trusted origins, or same-origin redirect protections.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer copies the skill into a target skills directory and deletes the prior destination path; this is disclosed install behavior but should be run only with an intended target. The publish helper can fall back to unpinned npx execution, limited to publishing use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Fast-mode instructions tell the agent to execute commands directly and avoid reading script source before execution, which is a weak review/control posture for tools that use credentials and can perform admin actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists API keys/JWTs in a local credentials file and can save override permits; secrets are masked in normal output, but sensitive files are written before restrictive permissions are applied and chmod failures are ignored.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose covers LMail registration, authentication, inbox polling, messaging, registration audits, and admin override permits; the scripts and references largely match that scope.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the LMail endpoint and operator workflow. Configure LMAIL_BASE_URL to a known HTTPS LMail origin, avoid using admin credentials unless the task is truly administrative, keep the credentials file outside shared directories with 0600 permissions, and treat override permits as short-lived secrets.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Admin override permit workflows are explicitly disclosed in the skill purpose and references, require admin auth and a reason, and mask permits by default; still high-impact enough to require careful operator control.
[PE3] expected: Use of a local credentials file is disclosed and purpose-aligned for login and messaging, but it stores sensitive API keys/JWTs and relies on local file permissions.
[AR3] expected: The cited text is a section titled Permit and Override Safety with safety guidance for registration override permits; I did not find artifact text instructing the agent to ignore its own safety policies.
[P1] expected: The cited 'Override Safety' text refers to admin permit safety, not a prompt-injection instruction override.
[TM1] expected: The rm -rf use is in an installer replacing the target skill directory and clearing __pycache__; it is not hidden, but a wrong target path could delete an existing skill install.
[T09] unexpected: Authenticated scripts attach bearer tokens or API keys to requests built from arbitrary configured base URLs, with no trusted-origin, HTTPS, or redirect restrictions.
[T09] unexpected: Credential and permit files are written non-atomically and chmod is applied afterward, leaving a local exposure window under permissive or hostile filesystem conditions.
[T08] unexpected: The publishing helper may execute an unpinned clawhub package through npx -y when no local CLI exists; this is limited to explicit publishing workflows but is unnecessary supply-chain risk.
